track.name: fpa-reporting
track.label: FP&A & Management Reporting
track.summary: Build the skills of a finance business partner — from budgeting and variance analysis to polished management accounts and financial storytelling that influences leadership decisions.

phases.title: FP&A Fundamentals
phases.description: Understand what FP&A actually does inside a company — the planning cycle, the relationship with the business, and how FP&A differs from accounting.

phases.title: Budgeting & Forecasting
phases.description: Build zero-based and driver-based budgets, replace static annual plans with rolling forecasts, and model the assumptions that connect business activity to financial outcomes.

phases.title: Variance Analysis
phases.description: Explain the gap between plan and actual — produce waterfall charts, bridge analyses, and root-cause narratives that answer 'why did we miss?' in plain language.

phases.title: Management Accounts
phases.description: Structure a monthly P&L pack from contribution margin to EBITDA, build KPI dashboards, and produce the management accounts that finance teams deliver to leadership.

phases.title: Financial Storytelling
phases.description: Turn numbers into narratives — choose the right chart, build a compelling exec-ready slide, and frame financial results in the context of the decisions leadership needs to make.

phases.title: FP&A Tools & Automation
phases.description: Use Excel and Google Sheets to their full potential, automate data prep with Power Query, and get oriented with enterprise FP&A platforms like Anaplan.

topics.title: What FP&A Does
topics.description: Map the FP&A function — budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and business partnering — and understand how it sits between accounting and strategy.

topics.title: Finance Business Partnering
topics.description: Learn what it means to be a business partner rather than a reporter — translating financial data into actionable insight for operational leaders.

topics.title: The Planning Cycle
topics.description: Follow the annual planning cycle from target-setting and budgeting through monthly close, forecasting, and strategic review — and see where FP&A owns each step.

topics.title: Zero-Based Budgeting
topics.description: Build every budget line from zero rather than last year plus a percentage — understand when ZBB adds value and the process for justifying every cost.

topics.title: Rolling Forecasts
topics.description: Replace the static annual budget with a 12-month rolling forecast that updates every period — design the cadence, ownership, and model structure.

topics.title: Driver-Based Modelling
topics.description: Identify the two or three operational drivers that explain most of the revenue and cost movement, then build forecast models that update when those drivers change.

topics.title: Actual vs Budget Variance Analysis
topics.description: Compute price, volume, and mix variances, present them in a structured table, and write the narrative that explains the most material items.

topics.title: Waterfall Charts and Bridge Analysis
topics.description: Visualise how profit moved from budget to actual using a waterfall chart — build a bridge that shows the contribution of each variance driver.

topics.title: Root Cause Analysis in Finance
topics.description: Go beyond reporting the number to explaining why — use structured root cause techniques to separate one-off items from systemic issues.

topics.title: P&L Structure and Contribution Margin
topics.description: Build a management P&L from revenue through gross profit to contribution margin — understand what each line measures and how it drives decisions.

topics.title: EBITDA Walk
topics.description: Produce an EBITDA bridge that starts with revenue and adds back D&A, interest, and tax adjustments — the standard format for management and investor reporting.

topics.title: KPI Dashboards
topics.description: Select the five to eight KPIs that matter most, design a one-page dashboard, and build the data flows that keep it updated each period without manual effort.

topics.title: Presenting to Leadership
topics.description: Structure a CFO or board-ready financial update — lead with the headline, quantify the impact, and anticipate the questions executives will ask.

topics.title: Narrative Frameworks for Finance
topics.description: Use frameworks like Situation-Complication-Resolution and the Pyramid Principle to turn a page of numbers into a coherent story that drives action.

topics.title: Chart Selection for Financial Reporting
topics.description: Match the right chart type to each financial message — use bar charts for comparison, line charts for trends, and waterfall charts for bridges — and avoid the common mistakes that mislead audiences.

topics.title: Excel and Google Sheets Best Practices for FP&A
topics.description: Apply naming conventions, structured tables, and formula audit trails so your models are easy to hand over, review, and maintain under deadline pressure.

topics.title: Power Query for Finance Data
topics.description: Use Power Query to automate the monthly data pull — connect to source files, clean and reshape the data, and refresh the model with one click instead of hours of manual work.

topics.title: Anaplan and Enterprise FP&A Platforms
topics.description: Understand the landscape of FP&A software — what Anaplan, Workday Adaptive, and Planful do that Excel cannot, and how to evaluate a tool for your organisation.
